question.text: A series LCR circuit is connected to an AC source of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math>. The circuit contains a resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>, an inductor of inductive reactance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>70</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>, and a capacitor of capacitive reactance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>130</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. The power factor of circuit is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is:

solution.text:
Power factor in LCR circuit is given by, 

cos ϕ=RZ, where, Z is the total impedance of the circuit.

So, cosϕ=RR2+XC-XL2

Putting the values, we have

⇒cos ϕ=80(80)2+(60)2

⇒cos ϕ=80100⇒810

Thus, the value of x=8.
